title: Berberine alleviates postoperative cognitive dysfunction by suppressing microglial IDO1 induction and kynurenine pathway activation in aged mice.
authors: Yang, Jialin; Liu, Xiaohong; Zhang, Tongtong; Wei, Yuqian; Xie, Shenyuan; Pan, Weidong; Lin, Wenjun; Zheng, Xiaochun; Yao, Yusheng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小檗碱通过抑制小胶质细胞IDO1和犬尿氨酸通路改善术后认知功能障碍，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白作用，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) is a common complication of surgery in elderly patients, and no pharmacological therapy has been approved. Although indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1)-driven kynurenine pathway activation has been linked to perioperative neurocognitive impairment, neither the cellular source of this activation in the hippocampus nor its upstream transcriptional control has been defined. In a tibial fracture model in aged mice, anesthesia and surgery raised hippocampal pro-inflammatory cytokines and IDO1, the latter predominantly in microglia, increased the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio, and produced cognitive impairment, dendritic simplification and synaptic loss. IDO1 inhibition with 1-methyl-DL-tryptophan attenuated these deficits, whereas exogenous L-kynurenine reproduced the cognitive impairment in surgery-naive mice, indicating that IDO1-driven tryptophan catabolism contributes to postoperative cognitive injury. Berberine improved cognition dose-dependently and attenuated the dendritic, synaptic and metabolic changes; at the effective dose it reached the hippocampus at concentrations 2.6-fold those in plasma. Network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation identified STAT3 among candidate transcriptional regulators; surface plasmon resonance demonstrated direct binding, a cellular thermal shift assay confirmed engagement of endogenous STAT3 in microglia, and an Ido1 promoter-luciferase reporter showed that berberine suppressed STAT3-dependent transcription. Microglia-targeted Ido1 overexpression attenuated the protection conferred by berberine, indicating that microglial IDO1 mediates a substantial part of its action. These findings identify the microglial STAT3-IDO1 axis as a candidate target for perioperative neuroprotection and support further translational evaluation of berberine in this setting.
abstract_zh: 术后认知功能障碍（POCD）是老年患者手术中常见的并发症，目前尚无获批的药物治疗。尽管吲哚胺2,3-双加氧酶1（IDO1）驱动的犬尿氨酸通路激活与围手术期神经认知损伤相关，但海马中该激活的细胞来源及其上游转录调控尚未明确。在老年小鼠的胫骨骨折模型中，麻醉和手术升高了海马促炎细胞因子和IDO1（后者主要在小胶质细胞中），增加了犬尿氨酸与色氨酸的比值，并导致认知障碍、树突简化和突触丢失。使用1-甲基-DL-色氨酸抑制IDO1可减轻这些缺陷，而外源性L-犬尿氨酸在未手术小鼠中重现了认知障碍，表明IDO1驱动的色氨酸分解代谢有助于术后认知损伤。小檗碱剂量依赖性地改善认知，并减轻树突、突触和代谢变化；在有效剂量下，其海马浓度达到血浆浓度的2.6倍。网络药理学、分子对接和分子动力学模拟将STAT3确定为候选转录调控因子；表面等离子体共振显示直接结合，细胞热位移实验确认了小胶质细胞中内源性STAT3的参与，且Ido1启动子-荧光素酶报告基因显示小檗碱抑制STAT3依赖性转录。小胶质细胞靶向的Ido1过表达减弱了小檗碱提供的保护作用，表明小胶质细胞IDO1介导了其大部分作用。这些发现将小胶质细胞STAT3-IDO1轴确定为围手术期神经保护的候选靶点，并支持小檗碱在此情境下的进一步转化评估。
